PROMPT 11 — ZAHHAK ASCENDS TO THE ROYAL SUMMIT

OUTPUT FORMAT:

Create one 15-second cinematic video.

Horizontal 16:9 landscape frame only.

The entire sequence focuses exclusively on Zahhak ascending through the Royal Summit Hall toward the elevated Royal Summit Platform.

The visual meaning of the sequence is absolute upward movement:

Zahhak is rising physically,
approaching royal power,
and becoming larger and more threatening with every step.

Every staircase must visibly ascend toward a higher architectural level.

Zahhak never walks downward.

Zahhak never descends a staircase.

No downward movement occurs anywhere in the sequence.


CHARACTER REFERENCES:

— CHAR_ZAHHAK:
[MENTION ZAHHAK REFERENCE IMAGE HERE]

Use this reference as the immutable identity, sculptural mask, royal costume, materials, body proportions and visual design of Zahhak.

Preserve Zahhak’s established height of approximately 178 centimeters, pronounced limp, heavy physical presence and controlled posture.

— CREATURE_ZAHHAK_SERPENTS:
[MENTION ZAHHAK SERPENTS REFERENCE IMAGE HERE]

Preserve the exact established black serpents, scale texture, anatomy, size and organic movement.

The serpents remain physically attached to Zahhak’s shoulders and move subtly with his body.

Do not multiply, remove or redesign them.


LOCATION REFERENCES:

— LOC_ROYAL_SUMMIT_HALL:
[MENTION ROYAL SUMMIT HALL REFERENCE IMAGE HERE]

Use this reference as the immutable architectural anchor for the entire sequence.

Preserve the vast enclosed royal hall, monumental interior scale, existing columns, walls, floor, staircase and elevated architectural levels.

No exterior space, sky or outdoor landscape is visible.

— LOC_ROYAL_SUMMIT_PLATFORM:
[MENTION ROYAL SUMMIT PLATFORM REFERENCE IMAGE HERE]

Preserve the exact elevated royal platform at the top of the ascending staircase.

The Royal Summit Platform must remain physically higher than the main hall floor.


PROP REFERENCES:

— PROP_ZAHHAK_SERPENT_STAFF:
[MENTION ZAHHAK’S SERPENT STAFF REFERENCE IMAGE HERE]

Preserve the exact design, material, scale and serpent ornamentation of Zahhak’s royal staff.

Zahhak uses the staff to support his established limp throughout the ascent.

The staff remains in the same hand in every shot.


DIRECTIONAL AND SPATIAL LOCK:

The main hall floor is the lowest architectural level.

The Royal Summit Platform is the highest architectural level.

The staircase rises continuously from the lower hall toward the upper platform.

Zahhak begins at the bottom of the staircase.

Zahhak finishes at the top of the staircase.

In every lateral composition, Zahhak moves consistently from the lower-left area of the horizontal frame toward the upper-right area.

Never reverse this screen direction.

The camera always remains below Zahhak, beside his ascent or slightly behind him.

Never position the camera in a way that makes Zahhak appear to descend.


SHOT 1 — ENTERING THE ASCENT — 0:00–0:04:

18mm extremely low-angle handheld wide shot from near the stone floor of the Royal Summit Hall.

Begin behind Zahhak and several meters below him.

The monumental staircase is fully readable as an upward architectural path.

Its lower steps begin close to the camera in the foreground.

The stairs rise steeply toward the elevated Royal Summit Platform in the upper-right background.

Zahhak enters the staircase from the lower-left side of the horizontal frame.

He plants the referenced serpent staff firmly onto the first higher step.

He transfers his weight through the staff and lifts his body upward.

His pronounced limp remains visible but does not make him weak.

The effort gives every upward step weight and authority.

His dark royal costume trails across the lower steps.

The serpents remain close to his shoulders, making small organic adjustments as his body rises.

The camera advances behind him from below without overtaking him.

Keep Zahhak’s body silhouetted against the ascending staircase.

Cut as his second foot reaches the next higher step.


SHOT 2 — POWER THROUGH THE BODY — 0:04–0:08:

28mm low side-profile handheld tracking shot from the lower side of the staircase.

Preserve Zahhak’s continuous upward movement from lower-left to upper-right.

The camera travels parallel to the stairs while remaining physically lower than Zahhak’s torso.

Show the architecture rising diagonally through the horizontal frame.

Zahhak drives the serpent staff onto a higher step.

His shoulder lowers briefly under his weight.

He pulls the rest of his body upward.

His costume stretches across his back and legs with the effort.

One serpent lifts its head slightly as Zahhak rises.

The remaining serpents move subtly with his shoulders.

Do not show hesitation.

Do not show weakness.

His limp makes the ascent slower, heavier and more intimidating.

The camera allows the lower hall to fall gradually farther beneath him.

Cut only after Zahhak completes another full upward step.


SHOT 3 — THE HALL FALLS BELOW HIM — 0:08–0:12:

21mm low rear three-quarter handheld shot from several steps below Zahhak.

Frame Zahhak against the upper architecture.

The Royal Summit Platform is now visibly close above him.

The lower hall remains visible far beneath and behind his body.

Zahhak continues climbing upward without stopping.

The camera climbs behind him but remains at least three steps lower throughout the shot.

With every step, more of the lower hall disappears beneath the bottom edge of the horizontal frame.

Zahhak’s silhouette becomes larger against the elevated platform.

The staff strikes one higher step.

His foot follows.

His body rises above another architectural level.

The serpents create a dark, living crown around his shoulders without changing their established design.

Do not orbit around Zahhak.

Do not move in front of him.

Do not obscure the upward direction of the stairs.

Cut as Zahhak’s leading foot reaches the final step beneath the Royal Summit Platform.


SHOT 4 — THE HIGHEST POINT — 0:12–0:15:

24mm monumental low-angle composition from the staircase below the Royal Summit Platform.

The camera remains on a lower step and looks upward.

Zahhak completes the final upward step and enters the elevated Royal Summit Platform.

He does not turn toward the camera.

He advances only one controlled step onto the highest level.

He plants the serpent staff beside him.

He straightens as much as his established body posture allows.

The lower staircase drops away behind and beneath him.

The enormous hall now appears subordinate to his elevated position.

Hold Zahhak at the highest point of the composition.

His masked head, shoulders and serpents form one severe silhouette against the upper interior architecture.

End before he sits, speaks, gestures or performs any additional action.

The final image is Zahhak standing above the hall after completing the ascent.


PERFORMANCE:

Zahhak does not rush.

He climbs with heavy certainty.

His pronounced limp remains visible in every shot.

The limp must never make the ascent look accidental, fragile or defeated.

Each upward step feels deliberate and irreversible.

He uses the staff as a physical extension of his authority.

His upper body remains controlled.

His masked head stays directed toward the elevated platform.

He never looks down at the steps.

He never looks back toward the lower hall.

The serpents move minimally and organically.

No theatrical villain performance.

No exaggerated aggression.

No triumphant arm gesture.

Power comes from Zahhak’s physical ascent, scale, weight and silence.


CAMERA AND EDITING:

Use exactly four shots totaling 15 seconds.

Every shot must clearly show Zahhak gaining height.

Keep the camera physically below Zahhak throughout the entire sequence.

Use low angles and wide lenses to enlarge his body against the monumental interior.

Preserve the same upward screen direction:

lower-left to upper-right.

Use controlled human handheld movement with subtle weight from the operator climbing behind or beside him.

The handheld camera must feel physically present but not chaotic.

No smooth commercial gimbal movement.

No Steadicam.

No orbit.

No overhead shot.

No crane movement.

No drone perspective.

No shot from the top looking down the staircase.

No reverse direction.

No camera move descending alongside Zahhak.

No cutaway to Jamshid.

No parallel editing.

No reaction shots.

No close-up that hides the upward staircase.

No slow motion.

No speed ramp.

No dramatic zoom.


LIGHT AND VISUAL STYLE:

Cinematic horizontal 16:9.

Dark, severe, monumental and physically believable.

Use only the established motivated interior light of the referenced Royal Summit Hall.

Allow the lower hall to remain darker.

The elevated platform receives slightly more cold natural or architectural light from the existing upper openings of the referenced hall.

The light does not magically change during the ascent.

Zahhak gradually enters the existing upper light because his body physically climbs toward it.

Preserve tactile detail in:

— black stone;
— worn royal fabric;
— the weathered serpent staff;
— sculptural mask surfaces;
— black serpent scales;
— the edges of the ascending steps.

Maintain restrained natural exposure.

Deep shadows may surround Zahhak, but the direction of every ascending staircase must remain clearly readable.

Do not make the scene glossy, heroic or decorative.

No red demonic lighting.

No magical aura.

No supernatural glow.

No smoke.

No fog.

No floating particles.

No symbolic markings.


SOUND DESIGN:

No dialogue.

No narration.

No music.

Use only restrained diegetic sound:

— Zahhak’s uneven but controlled breathing;
— the dry impact of the serpent staff on each higher stone step;
— the delayed weight of his uneven footsteps;
— heavy royal fabric dragging briefly across stone;
— subtle serpent scales moving against his costume;
— the deep natural resonance of the vast enclosed hall.

Each staff impact should echo from a progressively higher position within the hall.

The final sound is the serpent staff striking the surface of the Royal Summit Platform.

After that impact, hold only the quiet resonance of the hall.


STRICT CONTINUITY AND ACTION CONSTRAINTS:

Exactly one Zahhak appears.

Only Zahhak appears in the sequence.

Jamshid does not appear.

No soldier, courtier, guard, attendant or crowd appears.

Zahhak begins on the lowest level.

Zahhak continuously gains height.

Zahhak finishes on the highest level.

Every visible staircase rises upward toward the Royal Summit Platform.

Zahhak never descends.

Zahhak never steps downward.

Zahhak never reverses direction.

Zahhak never returns toward the lower hall.

The camera never implies downward travel.

The stairs must never appear flat.

The stairs must never slope downward in Zahhak’s direction of movement.

The Royal Summit Platform must remain visibly above the hall floor.

The serpent staff remains in the same hand.

Zahhak’s limp remains consistent.

The serpents remain attached to his shoulders.

No throne is introduced unless already present in the assigned platform reference.

No exterior architecture is revealed.

End immediately after Zahhak reaches the highest platform and plants the staff.

Established requirements for this subject:
- No human appears without a mask. Every person on screen, including nobles, gift-bearers, servants and background figures, wears a mask. A figure who is not a named character takes one of the masked caste looks in @REF-001/V02. Never show a bare human face.

<<<image_1>>> is Zahhak (CHR-001 V06); match it wherever Zahhak appears.
<<<image_2>>> is jamshid hall (LOC-019 V01); match it wherever jamshid hall appears.
<<<image_3>>> is Civilization Caste Board (REF-001 V01); match it wherever Civilization Caste Board appears.
<<<image_4>>> is Staff - Bronze Cobra (PRP-001 V01); match it wherever Staff - Bronze Cobra appears.
